accuracy.evidence: Every past form was checked against the Oxford Learner's Dictionaries irregular verb list: sat, sang, got, won, ran, dug, brought, thought, bought, sold, told, grew, threw, cut, put, hid, came, caught, went, found, ate, made. Curriculum placement was checked against National Curriculum in England English Appendix 2 (Year 2 simple past, Year 3 consistent tense) and Common Core L.2.1d, which names sat, hid and told. Hidden, grown and tolled are explained as different forms (participles need a helper; tolled is a bell), not as wrong spellings of the past.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets over-regularisation, the documented error in child language research (Marcus et al., 1992) and in KS1 writing: goed in the step 1 prediction, sitted, telled, hided, comed, catched and growed in the slip step and challenge. It also covers analogy errors (brang from sing/sang in the challenge and m7, thank for think), using the present in a recount ('go' and 'come' choices in the diary, 'hide is now' feedback) and confusing the simple past with the participle (hidden, grown in m6 and m8).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagirrpast works on the shape of irregular verbs: a letter-tile builder where only the right new vowel turns sit into sat or dig into dug, a 2x2 family sort by past ending (-ought, -old, -ew, no change), an over-regularisation hunt, and a recount diary. flagtense places sentences on a timeline and builds is/was + -ing; flagirrpl changes noun plurals. Swapping labels would not turn this into another topic's lab; lab_distinct passed under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child acts before being told: dropping sit into 'add -ed' returns 'sitted is not a word. sit changes: yesterday I sat', dragging e into sit returns 'set is not the past of sit', and a wrong family drop reads the past aloud ('Say it: yesterday I brought ... ends like brought'). The end-of-step summaries list the patterns just used (i → a: sit, sang, ran; e/i → o: got, won).

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each have a tempting regular option that the lab disproves: goed for go (the sort refuses -ed for sit, hide, tell), singed for sing (only a in the vowel slot completes it) and cutted for cut (the no-change family takes cut and put unchanged). Each reveal line repeats the learner's choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Twelve distinct wrong-answer messages keyed to the slip: sitted (ed), present sit (now), telled (ed2), tolled as a bell (double), hided (ed3), present hide (now2), run as a vowel-changer (vowel), jump as regular (reg), bringed (ed4), brang by analogy with sang (sang), goed accepted in writing (ok) and go as regular (reg2). Six questions rotate.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and simple verbs a 7-year-old reads (sit, sat, sing, sang), one pattern per paragraph; the validator's family readability limit passed. Lab tiles hold one word each at 19-24 px. The adult text uses the precise terms simple past, regular, irregular (strong) verb, suffix, over-regularisation and participle.

no_filler.evidence: No warm-up lines; the content gate found no banned phrases and explanation overlap stayed under 12% against every lesson, including Past, Present and Progressive Tense (411) and Irregular Plural Nouns. Each feedback line gives the right form and the pattern, for example 'tell is in the -old family: tell → told, like sell → sold.'

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 and 360 px Android screenshots of all 6 steps in dark and light: the verb card and the two bins fit side by side with 16 px labels, the sit tiles are about 60 px with 56 px vowel keys, the four family boxes sit in a 2x2 grid, and the diary keeps the done lines in view above three large choices. A real touch drag on iPhone 13 sorted play and sit and dropped a into sit.

accessibility.evidence: The walkthrough gate completed all 5 tasks with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13 and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Every drag has a labelled button below the canvas ('sit: change the word', 'Put a in the vowel slot', 'bring goes in -ought', 'Write went'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with each feedback line. The dark-theme 'drop here' hint was fixed to dark ink on its white slot.

sources: National Curriculum in England: English Appendix 2 Vocabulary, grammar and punctuation, Years 2 and 3 (simple past, consistent tense)
Common Core State Standards ELA L.2.1d (past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs: sat, hid, told)
Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, irregular verbs list
Marcus, G. F. et al. (1992) Overregularization in language acquisition, Monographs of the Society for Research in Child Development
